notes: Night 2 findings: (1) The shipping-delay hypothesis for the Dec dip holds for Fennel & Flint with a plausible lag — their on-time delivery crashed to 53.7% in November (from ~85-88% normally) and their bad reviews peaked the following month, December (14 reviews, 3.14 avg, 35.7% 1-2 star). But it does NOT explain Wiesgrund Wohnen at all: their delivery performance stayed strong all through Nov-Dec (90.9%, 93.8%) and they used 0% Albion Parcel every single month — yet they had an equally bad December (12 reviews, 3.5 avg, 41.7% 1-2 star). So there are two different causes behind what looked like one 'Home & Living dip,' and I need to find Wiesgrund Wohnen's actual driver. (2) The image-bucket report, run without the active-only filter this time, overturned my 'maybe they're just new/unfinished listings' theory: the 85 zero-image products are actually the OLDEST on average (1,136 days vs ~1,040 for others) and have fewer variants (3.4 vs ~5.5) — these are neglected legacy active listings, not pending-content new ones, and notably zero B2B merchants have any zero-image products (B2B is always at least minimally photographed). So the zero-to-one-image effect looks like a real, if small and old, content gap worth cleaning up, not a proxy for recency. (3) The bundle-user list makes the pattern obvious just from eyeballing the 50 rows: every single bundle-using merchant is in Beauty, Food & Coffee, Books & Stationery, Jewelry, Consumer Electronics, or Home & Living — none are Apparel & Footwear, Sports & Outdoor, or B2B wholesale, and they skew toward low-variant, giftable, small-revenue merchants. I want one clean aggregate to confirm this is a true vertical pattern and not an artifact of which merchants happened to print. Tonight: drill into Wiesgrund Wohnen's actual December driver at the product level, check whether both merchants' December dips are a recurring yearly pattern (like Cragsley's) or unique to 2025, and confirm the bundle-vertical clustering with hard numbers.

requests.title: Wiesgrund Wohnen December 2025: Product-Level Review Breakdown
requests.question: Since delivery performance doesn't explain Wiesgrund Wohnen's December dip, which specific products drove it?
requests.grain: one row per product, for Wiesgrund Wohnen only, among products with at least one approved review created in December 2025
requests.details: Filter to tenant = Wiesgrund Wohnen. review_count/avg_rating/pct_1_2_star computed over approved product_reviews with created_at between 2025-12-01 and 2025-12-31, per product. category_name from products.primary_category_id -> categories.name. units_sold_last_12mo = sum of order_items.quantity for that product's variants from orders placed 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 with status not cancelled, for context on whether it's a popular or niche item. Round avg_rating to 2 decimals, pct to 1 decimal. Order by review_count descending, tie-break by avg_rating ascending.
builds_on: Fennel & Flint and Wiesgrund Wohnen: Review Sentiment vs Delivery Performance, Monthly

requests.question: Is the December rating dip a recurring yearly pattern for these two merchants (like we found at Cragsley), or something new and specific to 2025?
requests.grain: one row per merchant per year, December only, for 2023, 2024, 2025

requests.title: Bundle Adoption Rate by Vertical
requests.question: Is bundle adoption really concentrated in specific verticals, and how strong is that pattern across the whole merchant base, not just the list of bundle-users?
requests.details: merchant_count = count of non-deleted tenants in that industry. merchants_using_bundles = count of those tenants with at least one product_bundles row where is_active = true. pct_merchants_using_bundles = merchants_using_bundles / merchant_count * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. avg_pct_products_bundled_among_users = average of pct_active_products_in_a_bundle (as defined in the Collections and Bundles Adoption and Merchants Using Bundles reports) across only the merchants_using_bundles in that industry; null/blank if zero users. Order by pct_merchants_using_bundles descending, tie-break by industry name.
builds_on: Collections and Bundles Adoption by Merchant
